what_it_does: GSAcc accelerates 3D Gaussian Splatting—a modern graphics technique that renders scenes by projecting billions of semi-transparent 3D blobs (Gaussians) onto the screen instead of tracing rays. Current GPU rendering has two bottlenecks: stages of the pipeline run sequentially (preprocessing must finish before sorting, which must finish before rendering), and storing all intermediate results uses massive memory. GSAcc enables speculation: it begins sorting and rendering work on Gaussians before preprocessing fully completes, by predicting depth order based on partial data. It also introduces a Gaussian-centric dataflow that executes all stages in parallel without storing intermediates, plus dedicated hardware for fast sorting and rasterization (converting Gaussians to pixels).
